submission.natural_language_explanation: The positive pole is a retrospective detector for the linking ' of' and/or the head token of a stock two-noun 'X of Y' compound term in its bare form (no determiner after 'of'): it fires strongest on quality of life (peaks 10-13 at both ' of' and ' Life'), then end of life, bill of materials, terms of service, quality of service, cost of living, depth of field and field of vision (4-10 at the peak), and quality of care and point of view (3-6), while the words alone are inert (' service' reads 0.6 alone but 8.5 in 'terms of service'). Membership is lexical, not semantic or frequency-driven: substituting a merely similar domain noun keeps only the weak ' of' response (quality of education 1.6-3.8 vs 10.4), and compositional of-phrases of other shapes stay at the floor (place of birth 0.1-0.9, state of the art 0.2-0.7, speed of light 0.3-0.6, cause of death 1.3-2.4); reordering ('life quality', 'service terms') kills the peak, a determiner after 'of' roughly halves it (quality of the life 4.0 vs 10.4), the hyphenated/glued spellings are the same feature and fire as strongly or stronger (quality-of-life 13.5, ease-of-development 10.0, time-of-flight 7.6, out-of-the-box 6.4, internetofthings 3.5), and arbitrary initialisms mostly stay at the floor (only the scanned stored strings fire: SIL OFL, R.O.C., BOD, BioFOG, nOTScale, POV).

Major Innovation Projects | Overview
Currently newborns get a “heel stick” test to screen for about 30 inherited, treatable metabolic disorders. What if screening were expanded to sequence newborns’ entire genomes? The five-year BabySeq project, launched in 2013 by Boston Children’s Hospital and Brigham and Women’s Hospital, will look at the impact of such screening and the medical and ethical issues involved. More on the BabySeq grant announcement.
The CLARITY Challenge (Children’s Leadership Award for the Reliable Interpretation and appropriate Transmission of Your genomic information) is designed to identify best practices for the analysis, interpretation and reporting of DNA sequence data, and to provide the most meaningful results to clinicians, patients and families. The first challenge focused on rare disease, with results published in Genome Biology. The winners of CLARITY I were announced in our Newsroom and in our science blog, Answers. A new challenge will be announced shortly.
Undiagnosed Diseases Network
An NIH-funded consortium of Boston Children’s Hospital, Brigham and Women’s Hospital and Massachusetts General Hospital is seeking to solve diagnostic “mysteries” and provide care to patients with unknown disorders, via careful clinical evaluation, genetic and genomic analysis, environmental exposure analysis, proteomics, metabolic studies, systems biology, and network medicine analysis. Launched in July 2014, the consortium is one of six new clinical sites in the NIH Undiagnosed Diseases Network (UDN).
Founded in 2008, the Manton Center is the first center solely devoted to studying rare diseases. Manton scientists are investigating the genetic causes of a variety of rare diseases with the goal of developing diagnostic tools and effective treatments. The center’s state-of-the-art Gene Discovery Core, which includes a disease registry and DNA repository, is now enrolling patients from all over the world.
Adverse drug reactions affect some 70,000 children annually in the U.S. In a new research study called InforMED Kids, investigators are taking pharmacogenomics to the hospital’s epilepsy, end-stage renal and IBD programs, where patients typically require multiple medications. Using genetic information, they hope to predict adverse reactions to medications, ultimately enabling clinicians to select individualized therapies. The InforMED Kids study will enroll 1,000 children, returning results to the children’s health care providers.
ReSeq, short for Research Sequencing, was launched in 2012 and receives requests from clinicians and researchers throughout the Boston Children’s Hospital for no-cost whole-genome or whole exome sequencing—including many “cold cases” that can now be solved with new technologies.

Virtually everyone who has visited the Scala project page has seen the info page for the Scala plugin for Eclipse. There are a few screenshots, an update site and very little instruction on how to proceed from there. Those of you who have actually installed this plugin can vouch for how terribly it works as well as the remarkable lack of usefulness in its functionality. It’s basically a very crude syntax highlighting editor for Scala embedded into Eclipse. It has the ability to run programs and compile them within the IDE, but that’s about all. Worse than that, it seems to make everything else about Eclipse less stable; somehow crashing random, unrelated plugins (such as DLTK). Needless to say, it’s often a race to see how fast we can remove the Scala Eclipse plugin from our systems.
The good news is that once you get the plugin installed, the preferences beaten into submission, and the UI bugs safely ignored, things become quite nice indeed. The new editor is vastly improved over the old one, and it’s easy to see tremendous potential in the project. Things are actually getting to a point where I would consider using the plugin rather than my current jEdit setup.
Of course, it’s hard to get a good idea of how a tool works until you see it in action. That’s why I took the time to put together a small screencast which illustrates some of the highlights of the new editor. I made no attempt to hide the bugs which cropped up during my testing, so this should give you a fair approximation of the current state of the plugin and whether it’s worth trying for your own projects. The screencast has been produced at a reasonably high resolution (1024×732) in both Flash and downloadable AVI format. Enjoy!
Great, thanks for providing the screen cast!
Note that the plugin is still being developed: “It’s still a little rough round the edges (2008Q1) but is getting more stable as time goes on.” So I think it will improve quickly.
Thanks much for the info. I’ve seen comments about the “new Eclipse plugin” but with no links, information, timelines, or anything. I wasn’t even sure if the one on the main web site was the old one or new one. This helps clarify a lot.
Nice to have this writeup, Daniel. Note that the NetBeans Scala plugin (http://wiki.netbeans.org/Scala) is coming along, slowly but surely–I’m testing it with the very latest daily NB downloads, though I hope it will be stable for NB 6.1. The author, Caoyuan Deng, also won one of the grants to develop his plugin for NB, and that has an August deadline; so I’m hoping for something good.
Also, some people at IntelliJ continue to work on a plugin (under the ASL; the repository is open so you can keep an eye on progress), but there’s not updated release and it appears that it will be targeted at IDEA 8, if it does get released.

The healthcare management field is growing just as quickly in Virginia as it is throughout the country, and there are 3 universities that offer Healthcare Management Masters Programs in Virginia to prepare students for jobs as healthcare administrators.
In order to break into this fulfilling and rewarding profession, potential healthcare management workers will need to pursue a graduate degree so that they stand out among the rest. A Master’s degree in healthcare administration or a related field can be a major asset for anyone interested in helping move healthcare practices into the 21st century.
The Department of Health Administration and Policy at George Mason University is part of part of the College of Health and Human Services. The department offers innovate undergraduate and graduate degree programs for students interested in beginning or furthering a career in healthcare administration, management or health informatics.
The graduate degree in health administration helps students prepare for leadership positions in hospitals, private clinics, nursing homes and insurance companies. The program at George Mason University offers specialization in subject areas such as Risk Management and Patient Safety, Executive Management and Physician Practice Management. Students will have access to top-quality instruction from some of the best teachers and leaders in the health management industry.
Graduates of the MHA program at George Mason University are expected to develop innovative and sustainable solutions for issues in the healthcare management industry. Expected learning outcomes include the ability to analyze and interpret data, use critical decision-making skills as well as access and understand software used in clinical and medical settings.
The Master of Health Administration degree is certified by the Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Management Education (CAHME).
The School of Business Administration at Marymount University is a top-quality institution that trains the next generation of business men and women to think critically and apply innovative solutions to long-standing problems. The School itself has been voted as one of the best business programs for military veterans in 2013 and 2014.
The MSHCM is a rigorous degree program that helps students prepare to enter the fast-paced healthcare management field. Students are encouraged to look at current policies in healthcare in order to develop answers for issues with the field in the future. They will become proficient in economic analysis, human resources management and more. Students must successfully complete 42 credits in order to earn their degree. In addition, they must also take on an internship as part of a capstone project. Marymount University has strong partnerships with local hospitals in order to help students find work experience and earn credit towards their degree.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The waiter set a platter of oysters on the table and uncorked a bottle of wine.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Everyday partitive ' of' (twice) with no stock X-of-Y compound; the hypothesis says the linking ' of' only fires as part of a listed lexical compound, so this is the same token in an ordinary sense and should sit at the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She spent the afternoon in a field of tall grass behind the barn, watching the clouds.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed tokens ' field' and ' of' appear adjacent but inside a non-lexicalized 'field of tall grass' phrase with an adjective after 'of', which the hypothesis excludes from its lexical membership list ('depth of field', 'field of vision'), so it predicts the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The hotel's room service arrived forty minutes late and the soup was cold.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token ' service' appears alone in an unrelated compound ('room service'); the hypothesis says the words alone are inert (0.6 alone vs 8.5 in 'terms of service'), so no peak is predicted.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She picked up a copy of Life magazine at the airport before her flight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The tokenizer gives ' of' | ' Life' back to back, as in the top example, but here ' Life' heads a publication name rather than the stock compound 'quality of Life'; the hypothesis is lexical about the compound, not about the word, so it predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: From the balcony the view of the harbour was spectacular at sunset.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' view' is a claimed token, but here it heads an ordinary 'view of the ...' phrase with a determiner after 'of' and is not the member 'point of view', which the hypothesis says it excludes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They were living in a converted warehouse on the edge of town.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' living' is claimed as a trigger token, but here it is a verb with no 'X of Y' compound around it; the hypothesis says the word alone is inert and only 'cost of living' style compounds fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The speed of light in a vacuum is roughly 299,792 kilometres per second.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis explicitly names 'speed of light' as a compositional of-phrase of another shape that stays at the floor (0.3-0.6), so this is a near-miss with the same linking ' of' and no peak expected.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The committee reviewed the quality of education in rural schools and recommended more funding for teacher training.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Closest same-shape near-miss: 'quality of' followed by a non-member head noun; the hypothesis says substituting a similar domain noun keeps only the weak ' of' response (1.6-3.8 vs 10.4), so no compound peak is predicted.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The clerk rang up the purchase at the point of sale terminal near the door.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A genuine stock 'X of Y' compound, but not on the hypothesis's lexical membership list (it includes 'point of view', not 'point of sale'); the lexical-not-semantic claim predicts this stays at the floor, which also separates it from the sister's right-edge designation account.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Their service terms changed without notice, and customers were furious.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'service terms' is the reordering of the claimed member 'terms of service', and the hypothesis says reordering the compound kills the peak, so this should not fire despite carrying both content words.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The life quality index for the region improved slightly last quarter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'life quality' reorders the strongest claimed compound 'quality of life'; the hypothesis says reordering kills the peak, so the same two words in the other order are predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Print your name, DOB and signature in the box at the top of the page.
adversarial_test_results.detail: An arbitrary initialism is predicted at the floor by the hypothesis, which says only the scanned stored strings (SIL OFL, R.O.C., BOD, BioFOG, nOTScale, POV) fire; the model splits DOB into ' DO' | 'B', so the sister's right-edge account would fire on the final 'B' (it reports 2.8 on 'B' closing DOB) while this hypothesis predicts the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lecture on quantum theory was delivered by Niels Bohr in 1927.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A proper name with no linking ' of' that the sister's account treats as a lexicalized designation (it reports 1.9 on ' Boh' closing 'Niels Bohr') but which is absent from this hypothesis's lexical list, so the hypothesis predicts the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The annual survey tracks quality of life indicators across all twelve districts.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: the top claimed compound 'quality of life' in a bare form (' quality' | ' of' | ' life') inside a novel, non-chat, non-code context; the hypothesis predicts a strong peak at ' of' and ' life'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Before you sign up, scroll to the bottom of the page and read the terms of service carefully.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: the claimed member 'terms of service' (' terms' | ' of' | ' service') in a new instructional context with different surrounding words, which the hypothesis predicts fires even though ' service' alone is inert.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Rising rents and fuel prices pushed the cost of living to a twenty-year high.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: the claimed member 'cost of living' (' cost' | ' of' | ' living') in a news-like context unlike the examples, predicted active at ' of' and ' living'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The engineer exported a bill of materials listing every screw and bracket before the build.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: the claimed member 'bill of materials' (' bill' | ' of' | ' materials') in an engineering context absent from the examples, predicted active at ' of' and ' materials'.

Cross-genre positive holdout: the hyphenated spelling tokenizes as ' quality' | '-of' | '-life', so the claimed '-of' token is present inside a Python comment; the hypothesis says the hyphenated form is the same feature and fires as strongly or stronger than the spaced form.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The photographer stopped down to f/16, and the depth of field widened until the whole valley was sharp.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: the claimed member 'depth of field' (' depth' | ' of' | ' field') in a photography context not present in the examples, predicted active at ' of' and ' field'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
The regional planning authority published its five-year assessment of the housing programme on Tuesday, drawing on household surveys, transport records and environmental monitoring data collected between 2018 and 2023. The report runs to two hundred and forty pages and is organised into six chapters: housing supply, transport connectivity, employment patterns, public health, education and environmental quality. Each chapter summarises the evidence, lists the indicators used, and notes where the data are incomplete.

On housing, the authority finds that completions rose steadily until 2021 and then slowed as construction costs climbed. The average waiting time for a social housing allocation increased from fourteen months to twenty-two. Officials attribute part of the delay to the conversion of former office buildings, which requires lengthy planning consents and, in several cases, remedial work on outdated electrical systems.

The transport chapter is more encouraging. Bus ridership recovered to pre-pandemic levels, and the new cycle network now carries an estimated four thousand journeys each weekday. However, the report warns that maintenance budgets have not kept pace with the expansion, and that several bridges in the eastern wards will need structural work before 2027. Residents in the outer suburbs still report long commutes and infrequent evening services.

Employment has shifted toward health and social care, logistics, and professional services, while manufacturing continues a gradual decline that began in the 1990s. Median household income has grown in nominal terms but fallen slightly once adjusted for inflation. The authority notes that the gap between the highest and lowest income deciles has widened, particularly among households with children.

Public health indicators are mixed. Life expectancy at birth has risen for the general population, and childhood vaccination rates have recovered after a sharp fall. At the same time, the report records rising demand for mental health services, longer waits for specialist appointments, and a well-documented shortage of general practitioners in the northern districts.

The chapter on environmental quality describes improvements in air quality near the ring road following the introduction of a low-emission zone, alongside persistent problems with noise and light pollution. Green space provision per resident has fallen slightly because of new development on the eastern fringe, and several wildlife corridors remain fragmented.

In its concluding section, the authority argues that the settlements built during the period have performed better than their critics predicted. Residents there report shorter commutes, better access to schools and more frequent contact with neighbours, and the survey evidence suggests that their quality of life improved measurably over the period. The authority recommends that future funding decisions weigh these outcomes alongside raw housing numbers, and that the monitoring programme be extended for a further five years.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context positive holdout: the claimed compound appears as ' quality' | ' of' | ' life' more than 400 tokens into a policy-memo genre unlike the chat and code examples, testing the hypothesis's claim that credit for the peak reaches far back into the context rather than depending on a short probe.
